correctness.rationale: Exact evolution scales the input by exp(-cs²/2); Euler at s=0 does nothing and the second step scales by M=1-ct(1-t). For centered scalar Gaussian laws, including the zero-variance point mass, W2 is the absolute distance between standard deviations, which uses |M|. The attainable multiplier interval is [1-c/4,1). If +r is not attainable, the interval is wholly above +r and the midpoint is optimal. Roots for +r and -r exist exactly when their respective quadratics have nonnegative discriminant; +r and -r roots are disjoint and the merged roots are counted once. The two threshold functions are respectively strictly convex with negative derivative at zero (and positive eventually) and strictly increasing; their indicated endpoint signs yield the claimed phase counts. At a negative root the shared-input particle discrepancy is 4r². For the residual, material acceleration is (lambda'+lambda²)x and is already a Wasserstein gradient; its half-norm is |lambda'+lambda²| sigma/2. Dilation to the terminal law scales a standard-deviation perturbation by sigma(1)/sigma(s), giving the stated propagated weight. At c=4 the unique equal-mass split satisfies 1/2<q<2/3: the first half has mass pi/8, smaller than the chord bound sqrt(3)/4 for the second half; the mass up to 2/3 is bounded below by pi/8+sqrt(7)/36>4/9, which is an upper Jensen bound on the remaining mass. Therefore the surrogate has strictly positive exact terminal error while the interior quadratic roots attain zero. For the perturbation, the exact roots at epsilon=0 are simple, hence persist by the implicit function theorem. Simultaneous small epsilon and positive delta give uniform convergence of weights and cumulative masses; strict increase of the limiting cumulative mass gives continuity of the median. The positive error persists, even though delta regularizes only the weight and not the ODE. No explicit uniform perturbation interval or finite-N failure of the source's local-surrogate theorem is asserted.
